newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian PM objects to 'peace' in Japan park.
newsitem.headline: Australian PM objects to 'peace' in Japan park.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard came under fire on Friday for urging the removal of the word 'peace' from a joint Australian-Japanese friendship park in the nation's capital, Canberra.
Howard backed the Returned Services League (RSL), which represents former soldiers, in its bid to change the name 'Canberra-Nara Peace Park' to "Canberra-Nara Friendship Park".
The Japanese city of Nara is twinned with Canberra.
The RSL said the name was insensitive because Japan had never properly apologised for its role in World War Two.
"The (name) would suggest that Australia as a nation has absolved Japan of her war-time guilt and of course we have not done that," RSL president Digger James said in a statement.
Howard backed the league. "In these sorts of matters the sensitivities of the RSL should always be given proper weight," said a spokesman for the prime minister.
But Canberra's municipal leader Kate Carnell said removing the word 'peace' might offend the city of Nara.
"The message that would be sent out would be the wrong message to the people of Nara," Carnell said.
The Mayor of Nara is due to open the park on April 22, three days before Anzac Day, Australia's annual day commemorating the sacrifices of its armed forces.
